name: Tucson
tagline: Desert Sunshine, Low Costs, and 350 Days of Blue Sky
description: Tucson is one of the most affordable cities in the American West, offering stunning Sonoran Desert landscapes, a UNESCO-designated food scene, and over 350 days of sunshine per year. Arizona has a flat income tax rate that keeps more money in your pocket, and housing costs are remarkably low compared to Phoenix and other Sun Belt cities. For FIRE retirees who love warm weather and wide-open spaces, Tucson is a hidden gem.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – varies by neighborhood; central and northeast areas are safest
quickFacts.climate: Hot desert with mild winters; summers exceed 100°F but humidity is very low

housing.description: Cheapest acceptable studio or older 1BR in a workable midtown area — Amphi, Miramonte, or near the University

dining.description: Mostly home cooking supplemented by cheap, excellent taquerias and Sonoran hot dogs

healthcare.description: A subsidized Silver plan on Arizona's ACA exchange, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600 for a single person; Pima County is one of Arizona's cheaper markets, though without the subsidy the full price runs about $800 a month. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance and gas — essential in Tucson's spread-out layout (Sun Tran bus and a short streetcar only)

entertainment.description: Free hiking at Sabino Canyon and Saguaro National Park, desert trails, community events

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable studio or older one-bedroom near midtown or the University, cooking at home most nights supplemented by cheap and excellent taquerias, and a paid-off car. Tucson's low rents keep this Lean budget unusually comfortable for a US metro — housing barely tops $950. Sabino Canyon and Saguaro National Park provide free outdoor recreation year-round. The main budget watches are summer A/C and the ACA Silver premium, which stays low only if MAGI is kept under the 2026 ~$62,600 cliff (Arizona has no state backfill).

housing.description: A decent typical 1BR in a solid neighborhood — midtown or the Sam Hughes edge

dining.description: Regular dining across Tucson's UNESCO-recognized food scene

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost low only if MAGI is managed under the ~$62,600 cliff (no Arizona backfill)

transportation.description: A reliable car with full coverage for desert road trips

entertainment.description: A Desert Museum membership, horseback riding, stargazing tours, a gym

2M.lifestyle: A decent one-bedroom in a solid neighborhood, dining out several times a week across Tucson's UNESCO-recognized food scene, and a reliable car for desert road trips. A Desert Museum membership, horseback riding, and good coverage all fit, with weekend drives up Mount Lemmon or out to Kartchner Caverns. The dry heat is real in summer, but A/C and pool access keep it manageable — a comfortable, low-cost desert life.

housing.description: A high-quality 1BR or small home in walkable Sam Hughes or West University

dining.description: Frequent fine dining at the city's best restaurants; wine tastings

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan; padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits disappear

transportation.description: A late-model SUV, premium insurance, road trips to Sedona and the Grand Canyon

entertainment.description: A country club or resort membership, golf, spa treatments, gallery openings

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality one-bedroom or small home in walkable Sam Hughes or West University, regular fine dining at Tucson's best restaurants, and a late-model SUV. A resort or country club membership, premium coverage padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff, and regular road trips to Sedona and the Grand Canyon are all within budget. Tucson's low costs mean this tier stretches far — a genuinely comfortable, affluent life in a desirable area.

5M.lifestyle: A luxury home in the Foothills or a custom hacienda in the Tanque Verde Valley with a pool, cleaning and pool service several times a week, and concierge medical coverage. Near-daily dining at the city's best tables, a nice SUV, and business class for longer trips are routine, along with a resort membership and art collecting from Tucson's galleries. Arizona's low taxes and Tucson's modest cost base leave real margin.

10M.lifestyle: A Catalina Foothills estate with mountain views, household help several days a week, and occasional private-chef evenings alongside the city's best restaurants, plus top-tier concierge care with Mayo Clinic access up in Scottsdale. Travel is first class, a premium SUV and car service handle getting around, and dining out never involves checking the bill. Tucson's low cost of living makes this budget genuinely lavish — roughly $189k a year — with enough margin for a second property, year-round travel, and steady giving to conservation and arts organizations.
